minutes.headline: Select Board unanimously appointed Brian Marple to fill a vacant Board of Assessors seat.
minutes.summary: A joint Select Board / Board of Assessors meeting opened with the Select Board interviewing and unanimously appointing Brian Marple to an open Board of Assessors seat until the next town election. The Board of Assessors then heard that the Department of Revenue had approved its FY2026 values, discussed ongoing Munis/Vision billing bridge problems, chapter land liens, a long-overdue neighborhood valuation review, and preparation for the upcoming tax classification hearing, catching up on a backlog of draft minutes before closing in executive session to discuss exemption and abatement applications.

votes.motion: Appoint Brian Marple to the Board of Assessors, term to expire at the next annual town election
Accept the minutes of July 16, 2025 as amended
Accept the minutes of August 13, 2025 without modifications
Accept the October 22 executive session minutes as amended
Adjourn the open meeting and enter executive session under Purpose 7 (M.G.L. c.59 §60), not to return to open session

budget_items.topic: FY2026 assessed value change by class (LA4 comparison)
budget_items.what_was_said: The LA4 comparison report showed the assessed-value change from last year by land-use code, including single-family and condominium classes, and a rise in the single-family parcel count.

budget_items.topic: Property value mix by class (classification hearing pie chart)
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor's presentation pie chart shows the share of town value held by residential, commercial, industrial and personal property.
New growth for fiscal 2026 came in well above the estimate used during budget season, attributed partly to one large industrial/commercial facility.
The assessors reported abatements approved this fiscal year and compared the count to prior years' approved and rejected applications.
The average single-family assessed value for 2026 was reported, a small rise from the figure used last year for means-tested purposes.
A property owner lacking a lien on chapter-land property will pay a fee to the registry of deeds so the town can record a new lien.
A warrant article raising the income limit for the 41A tax deferral program was approved at town meeting, effective for taxes assessed beginning fiscal 2027.

Money set aside last May toward outside help with the neighborhood study was instead moved into the salary administration line to fund a new, unrated, contract-based assessing-assistant position, approved at town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Cost attributed to prior lax assessing oversight
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said past reliance on a third-party assessing contractor without board oversight had cost the town money.
The average commercial/industrial value, which includes chapter land, was reported as higher than last year's figure.

budget_items.topic: FY2025 tax rate as finally set by DOR
budget_items.what_was_said: Last year's proposed tax rate at the classification hearing differed slightly from what the state ultimately assigned.

budget_items.topic: Cost of mailing tax bills more frequently
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member cited the cost of a recent town-warrant mailing and suggested mailing tax bills quarterly instead of twice a year would roughly double mailing costs.

transfers.description: Funds set aside in May toward outside help with the neighborhood-revaluation study moved into the salary administration line to create a temporary assessing-assistant contract position

decisions.decision: Enter real estate exemptions manually into Munis as an interim workaround while the automated Vision-to-Munis bridge issue remains unresolved, to meet the December 14 billing deadline.
Continue to propose a single tax rate rather than a split rate for the classification hearing, having found no significant change in the town's property-class distribution.
Gather other towns' Clause 18 hardship-abatement criteria before the next meeting or two so the board can draft its own criteria rather than deciding case by case.
Arrange a demonstration of new mapping software (compatible with the town's Vision system) that may offer field data-entry capability, before deciding whether to switch vendors.
Continue holding Board of Assessors meetings roughly twice a month in the evenings, for transparency and public viewing.

New member Brian Marple's initial role will be to observe, listen and complete required Department of Revenue training modules, open meeting law training and conflict of interest training before voting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board unanimously appointed Brian Marple to the vacant Board of Assessors seat through the next town election.
The Department of Revenue approved the town's FY2026 property values.
Assessors will enter real estate exemptions manually into Munis as a workaround, since the automated link between Munis and the Vision system is not working, to meet the December 14 billing deadline.
The board decided to again propose a single tax rate rather than a split rate for the upcoming classification hearing.
Funds set aside for a neighborhood valuation study were redirected at town meeting to fund a temporary assessing-assistant position instead.

why_it_matters: The single-rate versus split-rate choice determines how the tax levy divides between homeowners and businesses, and it will be finalized at the classification hearing.
A manual billing workaround ahead of a December 14 deadline is a risk point for getting tax bills out on time.

A property-class revaluation review that has not been done in 30 years, now getting a temporary staff position instead of a full study, affects how accurately individual assessments reflect current neighborhoods.
watch_next: The tax classification hearing, where the board finalizes the single vs. split tax rate
Clause 18 hardship-abatement criteria, to be drafted after gathering other towns' standards over the next meeting or two

reconciliation.summary: Where both records cover the same ground they agree — the unanimous Marple appointment and the open status of Clause 18 criteria and the mapping-software question — but each side holds a large block of material the other lacks entirely: ours carries specific figures (assessed values, abatements, tax rates, mailing costs) the official minutes never state, while the official minutes record a whole executive session (14 real estate exemptions approved), the website-review item, and a 41A wording correction that our recording-derived minutes never mention. The transfer for the assessing-assistant position and the prerequisites before Marple can vote are described differently enough in the two records that a reader should check them against another source rather than assume either is complete.
